newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka to import 700,000 tonnes diesel in '97.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka to import 700,000 tonnes diesel in '97.

text.p: Sri Lanka expects to import up to 700,000 tonnes of diesel this year, an official at the state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) said on Tuesday.

"We plan to increase gas oil (diesel) imports to 700,000 tonnes this year to meet increased power generation because of drought and also because our production is lower because of the 40-day refinery shutdown," the official said.
The Indian Ocean island imported 600,000 tonnes of diesel last year, up from the planned 300,000 tonnes because of drought, he said.

The chairman of state power utility Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB), Arjun Deraniyagala, said in January the CEB was urgently increasing thermal power generation to ride out a drought caused by the failure of northeast monsoon rains for the second straight year.
The CEB would cut dependence on hydropower to 57 percent of the total requirement by building more thermal power plants by June this year, Deraniyagala said.
The island now has an installed capacity of 1,135 megawatts of hydropower and 250 megawatts produced by using fuel oil, mainly diesel.
Deraniyagala said the CEB was confident of avoiding power cuts, which disrupted commerce and industry last year, because of increased thermal power generation.
Water levels in hydropower reservoirs, which supply 85 percent of the island's electricity, have fallen to dangerously low levels with the failure of monsoon showers.
The CPC's only refinery at Sapugaskanda, just north of Colombo, which can process 50-60,000 barrels per day, reopened last week after a routine 40-day maintenance shutdown.
